75	- Minimal option: commitar os registros dos filhos num commit que também mude o roadmap

77	- Rationale: mudar o roadmap depois da aprovação de um milestone a invalida (só o `status: done` do fechamento guardado é tolerado), então a ordem pedida é impossível; o bloqueio já existe no selamento e no fechamento
78	- Consequences: a run do roadmap lê um worktree sem os registros de review dos filhos; o revisor julga o roadmap pelo sujeito

I recommend approving: the change is sound and correctly scoped. I found three low-severity follow-ups and no blocker.

I could only run `pose artifact-check`; every other shell command (`go test`, `pose assess design`, `pose suggest review`) was denied. So the conclusions below rest on reading the code and on the sealed evidence, not on runs of my own.

## What I checked

**Producer and consumer.**
- The one place that produces `"child <ref> has no sealed review bundle[: why]"` is `review_bundle.go:1816`, in `reviewBundleChildren`.
- The new filter is `review_dispatch.go:1715-1718`. It only drops text that starts with `child ` and contains ` has no sealed review bundle`.
- Other child blockers still block in the worktree: `child … does not stand` (`review_bundle.go:1821`, `:1877`) and `child … is not closed` (`review_closeout.go:2671`, `:2692`).

**Sealing still refuses missing children.** The child blockers are added to the bundle at `review_bundle.go:547`. Sealing at the real head refuses any blocker at `review_bundle.go:2082-2083`. The filter only runs at `review_dispatch.go:841`, so sealing is unchanged, as the spec requires.

**Closing still judges the children.**
- `getCloseoutState` blocks while a child is not terminal (`review_closeout.go:2664-2672`, `:2686-2693`).
- Verification builds its blockers from the prepared bundle's blockers, which include the child blockers (`review_bundle.go:3567`).

**The fix actually takes effect.** The next check, `sealedInputsThatDiffer` (`review_dispatch.go:1656-1694`), compares sections, governed inputs and subject file digests, but not `Children`. So a worktree without the children's records no longer fails at a later step. The subject is still checked file by file at `:1679-1691`, so the reviewer still sees what was sealed.

**Test.** The new test keeps three other blockers and drops both child forms plus the delivery-integrity one. The sealed check `integration:pose-mcp/go/sealed-checkout-child-evidence-integration` passed.

**`pose artifact-check --strict`:** no error findings, only warnings about orphan files (paths with no spec claim) in the rest of the repository. It reported change set `cs-661cfc6ac8b2` with head `25b24ee9`, a different id and head than the brief's `cs-2909fe8e4f4e` / `6fbed268`. It apparently read the main repository's later state; I don't count this as a defect in the change.

## Findings

- **F1 (low)** `pose-mcp/internal/pose/review_dispatch.go:1717`: the filter matches on message text from `review_bundle.go:1816`, with no shared constant or typed diagnostic between them. If the text changes, the filter fails safe: the blocker comes back, it does not hide anything else.
- **F2 (low)** `.pose/indexes/validation-matrix.json:2610`: the check `sealed-checkout-child-evidence-integration` is classed as `integration`, but it is a unit test of a pure string filter. R2 (delegated dispatch for roadmap and milestone) has no end-to-end test; the spec already lists this as a known gap with a follow-up.
- **F3 (low)** `pose-mcp/internal/pose/review_bundle.go:1821`: a milestone child whose bundle is in the sealed commit but whose approval was committed later would show up in the worktree as `child … does not stand`. That is not filtered, so the run would still fail. For milestones this probably can't happen, because closing the child specs moves the subject head forward, but I have not verified it. The planned dispatch test should cover this case.

## Criteria

| Criterion | Result | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| assumption-integrity | passed | Verified: sealing, closing and the input comparison as above. Not verified: no end-to-end dispatch (F2), the milestone case (F3). Accepted risk: the roadmap reviewer doesn't see the children's records. |
| backend-concurrency | passed | `unit:pose-mcp/go/test`; pure function, no shared state |
| backend-contracts | passed | `integration:pose-mcp/go/review-subject-later-removal-integration`; no contract change |
| backend-input-errors | passed | `integration:pose-mcp/go/sealed-checkout-child-evidence-integration` |
